9	/-!
10	# The relative Picard functor of a curve
11	
12	For a scheme `C` over a field `k` (an object of `Over (Spec k)`) this file defines the
13	relative Picard functor of Grothendieck–Kleiman:
14	$$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(T) \;=\; \operatorname{Pic}(C \times_k T)\,/\,
15	  \operatorname{Pic}(T),$$
16	line-bundle classes on `C ⊗ T` modulo classes pulled back from the test object `T`
17	along the second projection. The quotient — never the absolute `Pic(C ⊗ T)`, which is
18	not even a separated presheaf in any useful sense — is the functor that étale
19	sheafification and the representability theorem consume.
20	
21	Products are the cartesian-monoidal product of `Over (Spec k)` (chosen pullbacks of
22	schemes): `C ⊗ T`, projection `snd C T`, whiskering `C ◁ g`, matching the vocabulary
23	of the challenge statement file.
24	
25	## Main declarations
26	
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picFromBase C T`: the subgroup of `(C ⊗ T).left.CechPic` of classes
28	  pulled back from `T` along the second projection.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPic C T`: the relative Picard group, the quotient by
30	  `picFromBase C T`, a `CommGroup`; `relPicMk` is the projection, with
31	  `relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff` the exact coset relation (a genuine range condition, no
32	  choice, no `Nonempty (≅)`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMap C g`: restriction along `g : T' ⟶ T`, descended from
34	  pullback of Čech classes along `C ◁ g`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicFunctor C`: the relative Picard functor
36	  `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat`.
37	-/

43	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
44	open AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme (CechPic)
45	
46	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
47	
48	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
49	
50	noncomputable section
51	
52	/-- The subgroup of Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` pulled back from the test object `T`
53	along the second projection. The relative Picard group is the quotient by it. -/
54	def picFromBase (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup ((C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :=
55	  (CechPic.map (snd C T).left).range
56	
57	lemma mem_picFromBase_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
58	    L ∈ picFromBase C T ↔ ∃ N : T.left.CechPic, CechPic.map (snd C T).left N = L :=
59	  Iff.rfl
60	
61	/-- The relative Picard group of `C/k` at a test object `T`: Picard classes on `C ⊗ T`
62	modulo classes pulled back from `T`. -/
63	def relPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
64	  (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic ⧸ picFromBase C T
65	
66	noncomputable instance (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : CommGroup (relPic C T) :=
67	  QuotientGroup.Quotient.commGroup (picFromBase C T)
68	
69	/-- The projection from Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` to the relative Picard group. -/
70	noncomputable def relPicMk (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
71	    (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic →* relPic C T :=
72	  QuotientGroup.mk' (picFromBase C T)
73	
74	lemma relPicMk_surjective (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
75	    Function.Surjective (relPicMk C T) :=
76	  QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective (picFromBase C T)
77	
78	/-- The exact coset relation: two Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` have equal image in the
79	relative Picard group iff their ratio is pulled back from `T`. -/
80	lemma relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
81	    {L L' : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
82	    relPicMk C T L = relPicMk C T L' ↔ L / L' ∈ picFromBase C T :=
83	  QuotientGroup.eq_iff_div_mem
84	
85	@[elab_as_elim]
86	theorem relPic.ind {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {motive : relPic C T → Prop}
87	    (mk : ∀ L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic, motive (relPicMk C T L)) (x : relPic C T) :
88	    motive x :=
89	  QuotientGroup.induction_on x mk
90	
91	variable {T T' T'' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
92	
93	/-- Pullback of Čech Picard classes along `C ◁ g` sends classes from `T` to classes
94	from `T'`: the well-definedness of `relPicMap` on the `H_T`-cosets. -/
95	lemma picFromBase_le_comap (g : T' ⟶ T) :
96	    picFromBase C T ≤ (picFromBase C T').comap (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) := by
97	  rintro _ ⟨N, rfl⟩
98	  refine ⟨CechPic.map g.left N, ?_⟩
99	  show CechPic.map (snd C T').left (CechPic.map g.left N)
100	      = CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left (CechPic.map (snd C T).left N)
101	  rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp,
102	    ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left, ← Over.comp_left, whiskerLeft_snd]
103	
104	/-- Restriction of relative Picard classes along `g : T' ⟶ T`: pull back along
105	`C ◁ g` and descend to the quotients. -/
106	noncomputable def relPicMap (g : T' ⟶ T) : relPic C T →* relPic C T' :=
107	  QuotientGroup.map (picFromBase C T) (picFromBase C T')
108	    (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) (picFromBase_le_comap C g)
109	
110	@[simp]
111	lemma relPicMap_mk (g : T' ⟶ T) (L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :
112	    relPicMap C g (relPicMk C T L) = relPicMk C T' (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left L) :=
113	  QuotientGroup.map_mk' _ _ _ _ L
114	
115	lemma relPicMap_id (x : relPic C T) : relPicMap C (𝟙 T) x = x := by
116	  induction x using relPic.ind with
117	  | mk L =>
118	    rw [relPicMap_mk, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id, Over.id_left,
119	      Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
120	    rfl
121	
122	lemma relPicMap_comp (g : T' ⟶ T) (h : T'' ⟶ T') (x : relPic C T) :
123	    relPicMap C (h ≫ g) x = relPicMap C h (relPicMap C g x) := by
124	  induction x using relPic.ind with
125	  | mk L =>
126	    rw [relPicMap_mk, relPicMap_mk, relPicMap_mk]
127	    refine congrArg (relPicMk C T'') ?_
128	    rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left,
129	      ← MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp]
130	
131	/-- The relative Picard functor `T ↦ Pic(C ⊗ T)/Pic(T)` of Grothendieck–Kleiman, as a
132	presheaf of commutative groups on `Over (Spec k)`. -/
133	noncomputable def relPicFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
134	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (relPic C T.unop)
135	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (relPicMap C g.unop)
136	  map_id T := by
137	    ext x
138	    exact relPicMap_id C x
139	  map_comp g h := by
140	    ext x
141	    exact relPicMap_comp C g.unop h.unop x
142	
143	@[simp]
144	lemma relPicFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
145	    (relPicFunctor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (relPic C T.unop) :=
146	  rfl
147	
148	@[simp]
149	lemma relPicFunctor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
150	    (x : relPic C T.unop) :
151	    (relPicFunctor C).map g x = relPicMap C g.unop x :=
152	  rfl
153	
154	/-! ## Naturality in the curve -/
155	
156	variable {C} {C' C'' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
157	
158	/-- Pullback of Čech classes along `g ▷ T` sends classes pulled back from `T` to classes
159	pulled back from `T`: well-definedness of the curve-direction map on the `H_T`-cosets. -/
160	lemma picFromBase_le_comap_whiskerRight (g : C' ⟶ C) (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
161	    picFromBase C T ≤ (picFromBase C' T).comap (CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left) := by
162	  rintro _ ⟨N, rfl⟩
163	  refine ⟨N, ?_⟩
164	  show CechPic.map (snd C' T).left N
165	      = CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left (CechPic.map (snd C T).left N)
166	  rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left,
167	    whiskerRight_snd]
168	
169	/-- Restriction of relative Picard classes along a morphism of curves `g : C' ⟶ C`,
170	at a fixed test object: pull back along `g ▷ T` and descend to the quotients. -/
171	noncomputable def relPicMapCurveApp (g : C' ⟶ C) (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
172	    relPic C T →* relPic C' T :=
173	  QuotientGroup.map (picFromBase C T) (picFromBase C' T)
174	    (CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left) (picFromBase_le_comap_whiskerRight g T)
175	
176	@[simp]
177	lemma relPicMapCurveApp_mk (g : C' ⟶ C) (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
178	    (L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :
179	    relPicMapCurveApp g T (relPicMk C T L)
180	      = relPicMk C' T (CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left L) :=
181	  QuotientGroup.map_mk' _ _ _ _ L
182	
183	/-- Naturality of the relative Picard functor in the curve: a morphism of curves
184	`g : C' ⟶ C` induces a natural transformation `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{C'/k}`. -/
185	noncomputable def relPicMapCurve (g : C' ⟶ C) :
186	    relPicFunctor C ⟶ relPicFunctor C' where
187	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (relPicMapCurveApp g T.unop)
188	  naturality T T' t := by
189	    ext x
190	    induction x using relPic.ind with
191	    | mk L =>
192	      show relPicMapCurveApp g T'.unop (relPicMap C t.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L))
193	          = relPicMap C' t.unop (relPicMapCurveApp g T.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L))
194	      rw [relPicMap_mk, relPicMapCurveApp_mk, relPicMapCurveApp_mk, relPicMap_mk]
195	      refine congrArg (relPicMk C' T'.unop) ?_
196	      rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp,
197	        ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left, ← Over.comp_left, whisker_exchange]
198	
199	@[simp]
200	lemma relPicMapCurve_app_mk (g : C' ⟶ C) (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ)
201	    (L : (C ⊗ T.unop).left.CechPic) :
202	    (relPicMapCurve g).app T (relPicMk C T.unop L)
203	      = relPicMk C' T.unop (CechPic.map (g ▷ T.unop).left L) :=
204	  relPicMapCurveApp_mk g T.unop L
205	
206	/-- The curve-direction maps are strictly functorial: the identity morphism induces the
207	identity transformation. -/
208	lemma relPicMapCurve_id : relPicMapCurve (𝟙 C) = 𝟙 (relPicFunctor C) := by
209	  ext T x
210	  induction x using relPic.ind with
211	  | mk L =>
212	    show relPicMapCurveApp (𝟙 C) T.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L) = relPicMk C T.unop L
213	    rw [relPicMapCurveApp_mk, MonoidalCategory.id_whiskerRight, Over.id_left,
214	      Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
215	    rfl
216	
217	/-- The curve-direction maps are strictly functorial: composition of curve morphisms
218	goes to composition of the induced transformations (contravariantly). -/
219	lemma relPicMapCurve_comp (g' : C'' ⟶ C') (g : C' ⟶ C) :
220	    relPicMapCurve (g' ≫ g) = relPicMapCurve g ≫ relPicMapCurve g' := by
221	  ext T x
222	  induction x using relPic.ind with
223	  | mk L =>
224	    show relPicMapCurveApp (g' ≫ g) T.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L)
225	        = relPicMapCurveApp g' T.unop (relPicMapCurveApp g T.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L))
226	    rw [relPicMapCurveApp_mk, relPicMapCurveApp_mk, relPicMapCurveApp_mk]
227	    refine congrArg (relPicMk C'' T.unop) ?_
228	    rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left,
229	      ← MonoidalCategory.comp_whiskerRight]
230

9	/-!
10	# THE RING CASE OF THE `pic⁰` VANISHING IS ZARISKI-LOCAL ON THE TEST RING
11	
12	The surviving obligation of the whole vanishing route to a `JacobianData` is a statement at
13	an **arbitrary** `k`-algebra `A`, in either of two interderivable spellings:
14	
15	* `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))` — consumed by
16	  `jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton` (`Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean:269`);
17	* ring-level field-point rigidity `hrigAff` — consumed by `jacobianData_of_rigidityAff`
18	  (`Pic0RigidityAffineReduction.lean:190`).
19	
20	This file attacks the **quantifier** rather than the content: both spellings are Zariski-local
21	on `Spec A`.  The input is the *separation* half of the landed Zariski sheaf property of the
22	plus construction, `PicEtAff.eq_of_away_eq` (`PicEtAffZariskiSep.lean:137`) — nothing is glued,
23	so the gluing half (`PicEtAffZariskiGlue.lean`) is not used.
24	
25	## What this is and is not — READ THIS BEFORE PRICING ANYTHING BELOW
26	
27	It is a reduction of the *test algebra*, not of the geometry, and it does **not** prove the ring
28	case.  Two things are load-bearing and were wrong in an earlier version of this header; both were
29	found by a fresh-context audit (`I-1657`, `I-1660`) and independently reproduced here.
30	
31	**1. AT A FIXED `A` the reduction is real: the ring case at `A` follows from the ring case at the
32	members of any finite covering family of localizations of `A`, and there is no route back.**  That
33	is what `PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away` and `rigidity_of_away` say, and it is the usable content
34	of the file.
35	
36	**2. UNDER THE OUTER `∀ A` IT IS NOT A WEAKENING AT ALL.**  The two `JacobianData` producers at
37	the bottom quantify their pointwise hypothesis over *every* test algebra — and
38	`Localization.Away f` **is** a test algebra, so the outer `∀ A` already covers it.  The converse
39	is one line with the trivial witness `f = 1`: `Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem` says `1 ∉ p`, and the
40	hypothesis at `Localization.Away 1` is an instance of the global statement.  So
41	
42	> `jacobianData_of_forall_prime_subsingleton`'s hypothesis is **logically equivalent** to
43	> `jacobianData_of_affine_subsingleton`'s (`Pic0VanishingRoute.lean:296`), and
44	> `jacobianData_of_forall_prime_rigidity`'s to `jacobianData_of_rigidityAff`'s
45	> (`Pic0RigidityAffineReduction.lean:190`).
46	
47	Those two producers are therefore **restatements, not repricings**.  They are kept because the
48	pointwise *shape* is what a local computation delivers, but a lane must not read them as having
49	reduced the obligation.  The general lesson, which cost this session a false claim: before
50	pricing a localisation-or-pointwise reduction as progress, try the converse with the trivial
51	witness — if it closes, the reduction only helps at a **fixed** base object, and the consumer's
52	quantifier decides whether that is any help.
53	
54	**3. The interface is NOT a local-ring interface**, contrary to what this header first said.  The
55	hypothesis is about `Localization.Away f`, and `IsLocalRing (Localization.Away f)` does not hold
56	(verified: instance synthesis fails; a basic open of `Spec A` is not a point).  A lane with a
57	genuinely local computation holds `Localization.AtPrime p`, and **nothing here bridges `AtPrime`
58	to `Away`** — that bridge is spreading-out, it is unbuilt, and it is the real remaining work on
59	this side.
60	
61	Seminormality is the other half of the story and it does not go away: see the measurement at the
62	end of this docstring.
63	
64	## The degenerate test ring: the site is not a counterexample, and that is ALL it is
65	
66	`hrigAff`'s antecedent is **vacuous** at a subsingleton `A` (there is no `k`-algebra map from
67	the zero ring to a field), so the hypothesis demands `q = 1` for free there.  That made the
68	subsingleton ring the cheapest potential *refutation* site for the affine spelling, and it was
69	recorded as genuinely unchecked (inbox `I-1655`, author addendum).  It is now checked:
70	`PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_subsingleton` proves the plus construction **is** trivial there,
71	unconditionally and with no genus or curve input.  So the site is **not a counterexample**.
72	
73	**CORRECTED after a fresh-context audit (`I-1658`), and the correction is the honest reading.**
74	An earlier version of this paragraph said this "settles the open question of `I-1655`".  It does
75	not.  At a subsingleton `A` the antecedent, the conclusion, *and* this file's own pointwise-local
76	hypothesis are all vacuous together — the section is the vacuous-hypothesis instance of
77	`PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime` below, since `Spec A` is empty.  So it tells a reader
78	nothing about whether `hrigAff` is inhabitable at any `A` with a **nonempty** spectrum, which is
79	what the `I-1655` addendum was actually asking.  Inhabitability stays open.  What the section
80	does buy is that a specific attack is closed, and the four steps below are reusable.
81	
82	The chain is four steps, each of which is about the vehicle rather than the curve: `Spec` of a
83	subsingleton ring has empty carrier (`PrimeSpectrum.isEmpty_iff_subsingleton`), hence so does
84	the product `C ⊗ overSpec k A` (project along `snd`), hence its Čech Picard group is trivial
85	(the landed `Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`, `Pic.lean:257`) and so is the
86	quotient `relPic`; and every étale cover of a subsingleton ring is again subsingleton, because
87	its spectrum maps *onto* the empty spectrum.
88	
89	## Main declarations
90	
91	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away` — **the reduction, `Subsingleton`
92	  spelling**: triviality of the plus construction at each member of a finite covering family
93	  of localizations gives it at `A`.
94	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.rigidity_of_away` — **the reduction, rigidity spelling**: the
95	  `hrigAff` clause at each member of the family gives it at `A`.  Note the direction the field
96	  points travel: a field point of a localization `S i` restricts to one of `A` by composing
97	  with `A → S i`, so the antecedent at `A` supplies the antecedent at `S i` and no lifting of
98	  field points is needed.
99	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_away` — the same reduction
100	  transported to the `pic0Subgroup` carrier the producers consume.
101	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime` — **the pointwise form, and the
102	  one a consumer wants**: no covering family in the statement, only a basic-open neighbourhood
103	  at each prime.  With `subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall_prime` on the `pic⁰`
104	  carrier, and `span_eq_top_of_forall_prime` as the `Spec`-level step (a mathlib lemma
105	  re-spelled, not new).
106	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_subsingleton` /
107	  `subsingleton_relPic_of_subsingleton` / `Algebra.EtaleCover.subsingleton_carrier` — the
108	  degenerate-test-ring chain, unconditional.
109	
110	## What was measured and did NOT work, so nobody re-runs it
111	
112	The obvious hope is that "local" is enough on its own.  It is not, and the reason is worth
113	recording: `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)` **is** available for a local `A` (mathlib's
114	`CommRing.Pic.instSubsingletonOfFiniteMaximalSpectrum`), but the obligation involves the
115	polynomial ring, and `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial A))` does **not** follow from
116	`IsLocalRing A` — measured, `exact?` fails.  Traverso–Swan is the reason (that identity holds
117	exactly for seminormal rings) and a local ring need not be seminormal.  So at a FIXED `A` these
118	lemmas move the obligation to basic opens of `Spec A`; they do not discharge it there, and the
119	remaining content is seminormality-flavoured rather than quantifier-flavoured.
120	-/

276	The reductions above take the covering family as an argument, which is the wrong interface for
277	a consumer: a lane computing `Pic` locally knows something *at each prime*, not a finite cover.

279	about `Spec` rather than about the curve:

13	# Base change for polynomial and Laurent polynomial rings
14	
15	For a commutative ring `k` and a `k`-algebra `A` we record the canonical algebra
16	equivalences
17	
18	* `polyBaseChange`   : `k[X] ⊗[k] A ≃ₐ[k] A[X]`,
19	* `laurentBaseChange`: `k[T;T⁻¹] ⊗[k] A ≃ₐ[k] A[T;T⁻¹]`,
20	
21	and compute their effect on the tensors `x ⊗ₜ 1`.  On such elements each equivalence
22	is the coefficient-change ring homomorphism induced by `algebraMap k A`: for
23	polynomials this is `Polynomial.map (algebraMap k A)`, and for Laurent polynomials it
24	is `AddMonoidAlgebra.mapRingHom (algebraMap k A)` (there is no dedicated
25	`LaurentPolynomial.map` in mathlib).
26	
27	The final two lemmas are the payload consumed by the scheme-level `ℙ¹` bridge: the two
28	`ℙ¹` chart maps `Polynomial.toLaurent` (`X ↦ T 1`) and
29	`Polynomial.eval₂RingHom C (T (-1))` (`X ↦ T (-1)`) intertwine base change with the
30	polynomial coefficient map.  These are pure commutative algebra.
31	-/

43	/-- Base change for the polynomial ring: `k[X] ⊗[k] A ≃ₐ[k] A[X]`. -/
44	noncomputable def polyBaseChange (k A : Type u) [CommRing k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
45	    (Polynomial k) ⊗[k] A ≃ₐ[k] Polynomial A :=
46	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.comm k (Polynomial k) A).trans (polyEquivTensor k A).symm
47	
48	/-- Base change for the Laurent polynomial ring: `k[T;T⁻¹] ⊗[k] A ≃ₐ[k] A[T;T⁻¹]`. -/
49	noncomputable def laurentBaseChange (k A : Type u) [CommRing k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
50	    (LaurentPolynomial k) ⊗[k] A ≃ₐ[k] LaurentPolynomial A :=
51	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.comm k (LaurentPolynomial k) A).trans
52	    (((AddMonoidAlgebra.tensorEquiv (M := ℤ) k A k).restrictScalars k).trans
53	      (AddMonoidAlgebra.mapAlgEquiv k ℤ (Algebra.TensorProduct.rid k k A)))
54	
55	/-- The final coefficient-change equivalence sends a `single` to a `single`. -/
56	private lemma mapAlgEquiv_single (n : ℤ) (x : A ⊗[k] k) :
57	    (AddMonoidAlgebra.mapAlgEquiv k ℤ (Algebra.TensorProduct.rid k k A))
58	        (AddMonoidAlgebra.single n x)
59	      = AddMonoidAlgebra.single n (Algebra.TensorProduct.rid k k A x) := by
60	  rw [AddMonoidAlgebra.mapAlgEquiv_apply]; exact AddMonoidAlgebra.mapAlgHom_single _ _ _

62	/-- `laurentBaseChange` on a monomial tensor `single n c ⊗ₜ 1`. -/
63	private lemma lbc_single (n : ℤ) (c : k) :
64	    laurentBaseChange k A (AddMonoidAlgebra.single n c ⊗ₜ 1)
65	      = AddMonoidAlgebra.single n (algebraMap k A c) := by
66	  simp only [laurentBaseChange, AlgEquiv.trans_apply, Algebra.TensorProduct.comm_tmul,
67	    AlgEquiv.restrictScalars_apply, AddMonoidAlgebra.tensorEquiv_tmul,
68	    map_one, one_mul, AddMonoidAlgebra.mapAlgHom_single, mapAlgEquiv_single,
69	    Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_apply, Algebra.TensorProduct.rid_tmul,
70	    Algebra.smul_def, mul_one]

72	/-- On `x ⊗ₜ 1`, Laurent base change is the coefficient-change ring homomorphism induced
73	by `algebraMap k A`. -/

9	/-!
10	# A CHART-TRIVIAL PICARD CLASS IS TRIVIAL WHEN THE OVERLAP UNITS ARE ALL COBOUNDARIES
11	
12	For a scheme `X` with two opens `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`, the Wave-5 tangent lane built both halves of
13	the two-chart comparison
14	
15	```
16	Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ ⧸ (im Γ(V₀)ˣ · im Γ(V₁)ˣ)  ↪  X.CechPic
17	```
18	
19	— surjectivity onto the chart-trivial classes (`Scheme.twoChartClassHom_surjOn_of_chartTrivial`,
20	`Tangent/TwoChartRepresentable.lean:301`) and the exact kernel
21	(`Scheme.twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff`, `Tangent/TwoChartCechPic.lean:321`).  Composing them
22	gives a **criterion** nobody had stated: if every overlap unit is a coboundary, then every class
23	trivial on both charts is trivial.
24	
25	That composite is what a computation of `Pic` on a two-chart cover actually wants to consume: it
26	turns a statement about the *unit groups of three rings* — pure commutative algebra, no
27	cohomology — into triviality of a Picard class.  Both inputs are general in the scheme, so this
28	is too: no affineness, no curve, no dual numbers, no field.
29	
30	## Why it is here rather than in `Tangent/`
31	
32	The two inputs were built for the Wave-5 `ε`-kernel computation and live there.  This file is
33	about the *Picard group of a two-chart scheme* rather than about tangent spaces, and its intended
34	consumer is the ring-case obligation of the representability route
35	(`Picard/Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean`), where the relevant `X` is a relative curve over a test ring
36	and the three rings are the two chart algebras and their overlap.
37	
38	## The one hypothesis that is not about units
39	
40	`hsel`, surjectivity of the selector, is what makes the two-chart cover *honest* (both charts are
41	actually used).  It is not an extra obligation:
42	`Scheme.AffineTwoCover.surjective_selector_of_not_isAffine`
43	(`Tangent/TwoChartHonest.lean:108`) derives it from `¬ IsAffine X` alone, and a proper
44	positive-dimensional scheme over a field is not affine.  Stated with `hsel` explicit because this
45	file is general in `X` and the non-affineness is the consumer's to supply.
46	
47	## Main declarations
48	
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary` — the
50	  criterion.
51	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subsingleton_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary` — the same as a
52	  statement about the subgroup of chart-trivial classes, for a consumer holding two classes
53	  rather than one.

68	/-- The coboundary subgroup of the overlap units of a two-chart cover: the units of
69	`Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)` that are products of restrictions of chart units.  Abbreviation for the
70	`TruncExpCech` subgroup at the two restriction maps, so that the statements below read. -/
71	noncomputable abbrev twoChartCoboundaryUnits (V : Bool → X.Opens) :
72	    Subgroup Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ :=
73	  TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
74	    (X.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false))
75	    (X.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true))
76	
77	/-- **THE CRITERION**: on a two-chart cover whose overlap units are *all* coboundaries, a Picard
78	class trivial on both charts is trivial.

80	Composite of the two landed halves of the two-chart comparison: surjectivity presents the class
81	as `twoChartClassHom` of an overlap unit, and the kernel description kills it because that unit

88	    (sel : X → Bool) (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel)
89	    (hcob : ∀ u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ, u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits V)

101	    (sel : X → Bool) (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel)

103	    {L M : X.CechPic}
104	    (hL : ∀ s : Bool, Scheme.CechPic.map (V s).ι L = 1)
105	    (hM : ∀ s : Bool, Scheme.CechPic.map (V s).ι M = 1) :
106	    L = M := by

108	    cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary sel hmem hsel hcob M hM]
109	
110	/-- The criterion with `hsel` discharged from non-affineness, which is how a curve consumer meets

112	`surjective_selector_of_not_isAffine` turns that single fact into the selector surjectivity.
113

117	    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (D : Y.AffineTwoCover) (hY : ¬ IsAffine Y)

121	    L = 1 :=
122	  cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary D.selector D.selector_mem
123	    (D.surjective_selector_of_not_isAffine hY) hcob L hL
124	
125	/-! ## The form with a payable hypothesis
126	
127	The universal hypothesis `hcob` above is **false** at the case the representability route cares
128	about: for `ℙ¹` over a domain, `t` is an overlap unit and is not a coboundary
129	(`not_tUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits`, `Picard/LaurentTwoChartCoboundary.lean`) — which is just
130	`Pic(ℙ¹_A) = ℤ`.  So a consumer given only the criterion above would set out to prove something
131	untrue.
132	
133	The repair is to constrain only the units that *present the class in question*, which is what
134	surjectivity hands over anyway.  Two things are worth saying about it explicitly, because the
135	obvious repair is a trap:
136	
137	* the `↔` version — "`L = 1` iff some presenting unit is a coboundary" — is **vacuous**: its
138	  forward direction takes the presenting unit to be `1`, and the chart-triviality hypothesis is
139	  never consulted (measured: the unused-variable linter flags it).  So the useful form is the
140	  implication with a `∀` over presenting units, below, where both hypotheses are consumed;
141	* that form is *strictly weaker* than `hcob`, and demonstrably so: `hcob` implies it by ignoring
142	  the presentation equation (`forall_presenting_of_forall_coboundary`). -/
143	
144	/-- **THE CRITERION WITH A PAYABLE HYPOTHESIS**: a chart-trivial class is trivial as soon as
145	*every unit presenting it* is a coboundary.
146	
147	Both hypotheses are consumed — `hL` produces the presenting unit through surjectivity, and
148	`hpres` is applied to exactly that unit.  Unlike the universal form this is not refuted by
149	`ℙ¹`: there the presenting units of a *degree-zero* class are the exponent-zero Laurent units,
150	which are precisely the coboundaries (`mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff`). -/
151	theorem cechPic_eq_one_of_forall_presenting_coboundary
152	    (sel : X → Bool) (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel)
153	    (L : X.CechPic) (hL : ∀ s : Bool, Scheme.CechPic.map (V s).ι L = 1)
154	    (hpres : ∀ u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ,
155	      twoChartClassHom V sel hmem u = L → u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits V) :
156	    L = 1 := by
157	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := twoChartClassHom_surjOn_of_chartTrivial sel hmem L hL
158	  rw [← hu]
159	  exact (twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff V sel hmem hsel u).mpr (hpres u hu)
160	
161	/-- The universal hypothesis implies the presenting-unit one, by ignoring the presentation
162	equation.  Recorded so that "strictly weaker" is a proved relation rather than a reading of the
163	two statements — the weakening is what makes the hypothesis payable at `ℙ¹`. -/
164	theorem forall_presenting_of_forall_coboundary
165	    (sel : X → Bool) (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x))
166	    (hcob : ∀ u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ, u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits V)
167	    (L : X.CechPic) :
168	    ∀ u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ,
169	      twoChartClassHom V sel hmem u = L → u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits V :=
170	  fun u _ => hcob u

12	
13	The pure-algebra layer (`Picard/LaurentTwoChartCoboundary.lean` and the `Algebra/Laurent*`

17	instead holds `Scheme.twoChartCoboundaryUnits V`, the coboundary subgroup of the scheme
18	restriction maps `X.resHom` on `Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ`.
19	
20	Both are literally `TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits` of the respective restriction ring homs
21	(`Scheme.twoChartCoboundaryUnits` unfolds to it by definition, `LaurentTwoChartCoboundary.lean`
22	and `TwoChartCechPicTrivial.lean:71`).  So an **identification of the two data** — ring
23	isomorphisms of the two chart section rings with `A[t]` and of the overlap section ring with
24	`A[T;T⁻¹]`, intertwining the scheme restrictions with `toLaurent`/`rightChart` — transports
25	coboundary membership between them.  This file is that seam: it consumes the identification as
26	hypotheses (the base-changed `ℙ¹_A` two-chart cover that realises them is the remaining scheme
27	build) and hands back the scheme-side `twoChartCoboundaryUnits` membership the criterion wants.
28	
29	Nothing here assumes the identifying isomorphisms are anything in particular, and nothing here
30	uses a new hypothesis on the ring `A`: it is the naturality of `cechCoboundaryUnits`
31	(`TruncExpCech.mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_map_iff`) instantiated at the two Laurent chart maps.
32	
33	## Main declarations
34	
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_twoChartCoboundaryUnits_iff_laurent` — given the chart identification
36	  data, a scheme overlap unit is in `twoChartCoboundaryUnits V` iff its `A[T;T⁻¹]ˣ` image is in
37	  `laurentCoboundaryUnits A`.

49	
50	/-- **The algebra→scheme coboundary seam.**
51	
52	Suppose the two-chart cover `V` of `X` is Laurent-identified over `A`: ring isomorphisms
53	`γ₀ : Γ(X, V false) ≃+* A[t]`, `γ₁ : Γ(X, V true) ≃+* A[t]` of the two chart section rings and
54	`γ₀₁ : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true) ≃+* A[T;T⁻¹]` of the overlap section ring, intertwining the
55	scheme restrictions `X.resHom` with the two Laurent chart maps
56	(`Polynomial.toLaurent`, `rightChart A`):
57	
58	* `hres₀ : γ₀₁ ∘ resHom(inf_le_left) = toLaurent ∘ γ₀`;
59	* `hres₁ : γ₀₁ ∘ resHom(inf_le_right) = rightChart A ∘ γ₁`.
60	
61	Then a scheme overlap unit `u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ` is a two-chart coboundary iff its
62	image `Units.map γ₀₁ u : (A[T;T⁻¹])ˣ` is a Laurent coboundary.  Composed with the landed
63	`mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff_general`, this reads the scheme-side coboundary condition off
64	the exponent-zero normal form of the transported Laurent unit — with no new hypothesis. -/

66	    (γ₀ : Γ(X, V false) ≃+* Polynomial A) (γ₁ : Γ(X, V true) ≃+* Polynomial A)

70	      = (Polynomial.toLaurent : Polynomial A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).comp
71	        (γ₀ : Γ(X, V false) →+* Polynomial A))
72	    (hres₁ : (γ₀₁ : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true) →+* LaurentPolynomial A).comp
73	        (X.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true))
74	      = (rightChart A).comp (γ₁ : Γ(X, V true) →+* Polynomial A))
75	    (u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) :
76	    u ∈ Scheme.twoChartCoboundaryUnits V
77	      ↔ Units.map (γ₀₁ : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true) →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom u

81	      (X.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false))
82	      (X.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true))
83	      (Polynomial.toLaurent : Polynomial A →+* LaurentPolynomial A) (rightChart A)
84	      γ₀ γ₁ γ₀₁ hres₀ hres₁ u

8	/-!
9	# The Laurent chart pair on the projective line
10	
11	Continuation of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.P1`: the overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)` of the two standard
12	charts of `P1 k` and its identification with the Laurent polynomial ring, the section-level
13	chart identifications, and the bundled chart package.
14	
15	* `P1.overlapAlgEquiv : (k[X₀,X₁]_(X₀X₁))₀ ≃ₐ[k] k[T,T⁻¹]`, with the two restriction maps
16	  `P1.awayToOverlapLeft/Right` becoming `t ↦ T` and `t ↦ T⁻¹`
17	  (`P1.overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft`/`Right`);
18	* the *Laurent span* property `P1.exists_awayToOverlap_add`: every element of the overlap
19	  ring is a sum of restrictions from the two charts;
20	* section-level versions of all of the above (`P1.chartSectionsEquiv₀/₁`,
21	  `P1.overlapSectionsEquiv`, `P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_res_left/right`);
22	* the package `AlgebraicGeometry.LaurentChartPair` with canonical term
23	  `P1.laurentChartPair k`, and the span property `LaurentChartPair.exists_res_add_res`
24	  for any such package. This package is exactly what the two-lattice finiteness argument
25	  for `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` consumes.
26	-/

28	set_option autoImplicit false

40	variable (k : Type u) [Field k]

42	/-- The standard grading of `k[X₀, X₁]`, the graded ring underlying `P1 k`. -/
43	local notation "𝒜" => homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k
44	
45	/-! ### The overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)` and the identification with Laurent polynomials -/
46	
47	/-- The restriction map from the chart `D₊(X₀)` to the overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)`. -/
48	noncomputable def awayToOverlapLeft :
49	    Away 𝒜 (X 0) →+* Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) :=
50	  awayMap 𝒜 (X_mem k 1) rfl
51	
52	/-- The restriction map from the chart `D₊(X₁)` to the overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)`. -/
53	noncomputable def awayToOverlapRight :
54	    Away 𝒜 (X 1) →+* Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) :=
55	  awayMap 𝒜 (X_mem k 0) (mul_comm (X 0) (X 1))
56	
57	theorem awayToOverlapLeft_eq :
58	    awayToOverlapLeft k = awayMap 𝒜 (X_mem k 1)
59	      (rfl : (X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1 = X 0 * X 1) :=
60	  rfl
61	
62	theorem awayToOverlapRight_eq :
63	    awayToOverlapRight k = awayMap 𝒜 (X_mem k 0) (mul_comm (X 0) (X 1)) :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	theorem awayToOverlapLeft_algebraMap (r : k) :
67	    awayToOverlapLeft k (algebraMap k _ r) = algebraMap k _ r :=
68	  awayMap_fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 (X_mem k 1)
69	    (rfl : (X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1 = X 0 * X 1) (algebraMap k (𝒜 0) r)
70	
71	theorem awayToOverlapRight_algebraMap (r : k) :
72	    awayToOverlapRight k (algebraMap k _ r) = algebraMap k _ r :=
73	  awayMap_fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 (X_mem k 0) (mul_comm (X 0) (X 1))
74	    (algebraMap k (𝒜 0) r)
75	
76	noncomputable instance : Algebra (Away 𝒜 (X 0)) (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) :=
77	  (awayToOverlapLeft k).toAlgebra
78	
79	noncomputable instance : Algebra (Away 𝒜 (X 1)) (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) :=
80	  (awayToOverlapRight k).toAlgebra
81	
82	theorem isLocalizationElem_eq :
83	    Away.isLocalizationElem (X_mem k 0) (X_mem k 1) = chartCoord k 0 1 := by
84	  rw [Away.isLocalizationElem, chartCoord_eq]
85	  congr 1
86	  exact pow_one _
87	
88	/-- The overlap ring is the localization of the chart ring `(k[X₀,X₁]_(X₀))₀ = k[t]` away
89	from the chart coordinate `t = X₁/X₀`. -/
90	instance : IsLocalization.Away (chartCoord k 0 1) (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) := by
91	  have h : IsLocalization.Away (Away.isLocalizationElem (X_mem k 0) (X_mem k 1))
92	      (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) :=
93	    Away.isLocalization_mul (X_mem k 0) (X_mem k 1)
94	      (rfl : (X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1 = X 0 * X 1) one_ne_zero
95	  rwa [isLocalizationElem_eq] at h
96	
97	/-- The overlap identification as a ring equivalence; see `P1.overlapAlgEquiv` for the
98	`k`-algebra version. -/
99	noncomputable def overlapRingEquiv :
100	    Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) ≃+* LaurentPolynomial k :=
101	  IsLocalization.ringEquivOfRingEquiv (M := Submonoid.powers (chartCoord k 0 1))
102	    (T := Submonoid.powers (Polynomial.X : Polynomial k))
103	    (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) (LaurentPolynomial k)
104	    (awayAlgEquiv k fin_zero_ne_one).toRingEquiv
105	    (by rw [Submonoid.map_powers]
106	        exact congrArg _ (awayAlgEquiv_chartCoord k fin_zero_ne_one))
107	
108	theorem overlapRingEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft (z : Away 𝒜 (X 0)) :
109	    overlapRingEquiv k (awayToOverlapLeft k z) =
110	      Polynomial.toLaurent (awayAlgEquiv k fin_zero_ne_one z) := by
111	  rw [← LaurentPolynomial.algebraMap_eq_toLaurent]
112	  exact IsLocalization.ringEquivOfRingEquiv_eq _ _
113	
114	/-- The overlap identification: the section ring `(k[X₀,X₁]_(X₀X₁))₀` of the chart overlap is
115	the ring of Laurent polynomials over `k`, with `T = X₁/X₀`. -/
116	noncomputable def overlapAlgEquiv :
117	    Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) ≃ₐ[k] LaurentPolynomial k :=
118	  { overlapRingEquiv k with
119	    commutes' := fun r => by
120	      change overlapRingEquiv k (algebraMap k _ r) = _
121	      rw [← awayToOverlapLeft_algebraMap, overlapRingEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft,
122	        AlgEquiv.commutes, ← Polynomial.C_eq_algebraMap, Polynomial.toLaurent_C,
123	        LaurentPolynomial.C_eq_algebraMap] }
124	
125	theorem overlapAlgEquiv_apply (z : Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) :
126	    overlapAlgEquiv k z = overlapRingEquiv k z :=
127	  rfl
128	
129	/-- Through the chart identifications, the left restriction map to the overlap is the
130	canonical map `k[t] → k[T,T⁻¹]`, `t ↦ T`. -/
131	theorem overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft (z : Away 𝒜 (X 0)) :
132	    overlapAlgEquiv k (awayToOverlapLeft k z) =
133	      Polynomial.toLaurent (awayAlgEquiv k fin_zero_ne_one z) :=
134	  overlapRingEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft k z
135	
136	theorem awayToOverlap_mul_eq_one :
137	    awayToOverlapLeft k (chartCoord k 0 1) * awayToOverlapRight k (chartCoord k 1 0) = 1 := by
138	  rw [awayToOverlapLeft_eq, awayToOverlapRight_eq, chartCoord_eq k 0 1, chartCoord_eq k 1 0,
139	    awayMap_mk, awayMap_mk, ext_iff_val, val_mul, val_one, Away.val_mk, Away.val_mk,
140	    Localization.mk_mul, ← Localization.mk_one, Localization.mk_eq_mk_iff,
141	    Localization.r_iff_exists]
142	  exact ⟨1, by push_cast; ring⟩
143	
144	theorem overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapRight_chartCoord :
145	    overlapAlgEquiv k (awayToOverlapRight k (chartCoord k 1 0)) = LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) := by
146	  have h1 : (LaurentPolynomial.T 1 : LaurentPolynomial k) *
147	      overlapAlgEquiv k (awayToOverlapRight k (chartCoord k 1 0)) = 1 := by
148	    rw [show (LaurentPolynomial.T 1 : LaurentPolynomial k) = Polynomial.toLaurent Polynomial.X
149	        from Polynomial.toLaurent_X.symm,
150	      ← awayAlgEquiv_chartCoord k fin_zero_ne_one,
151	      ← overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft, ← map_mul, awayToOverlap_mul_eq_one, map_one]
152	  calc overlapAlgEquiv k (awayToOverlapRight k (chartCoord k 1 0))
153	      = (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) * LaurentPolynomial.T 1) *
154	          overlapAlgEquiv k (awayToOverlapRight k (chartCoord k 1 0)) := by
155	        rw [← LaurentPolynomial.T_add, neg_add_cancel, LaurentPolynomial.T_zero, one_mul]
156	    _ = LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) := by rw [mul_assoc, h1, mul_one]
157	
158	/-- Through the chart identifications, the right restriction map to the overlap is the map
159	`k[t] → k[T,T⁻¹]`, `t ↦ T⁻¹`. -/
160	theorem overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapRight (z : Away 𝒜 (X 1)) :
161	    overlapAlgEquiv k (awayToOverlapRight k z) =
162	      Polynomial.aeval (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k)
163	        (awayAlgEquiv k fin_one_ne_zero z) := by
164	  obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := polyToAway_surjective k fin_one_ne_zero z
165	  rw [awayAlgEquiv_polyToAway]
166	  induction p using Polynomial.induction_on' with
167	  | add f g hf hg => simp only [map_add, hf, hg]
168	  | monomial n a =>
169	    simp only [polyToAway_monomial, map_mul, map_pow,
170	      overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapRight_chartCoord, awayToOverlapRight_algebraMap,
171	      AlgEquiv.commutes, Polynomial.aeval_monomial]
172	
173	/-! ### The Laurent span property on the overlap -/
174	
175	/-- **Laurent span, ring level**: every element of the overlap ring is the sum of a
176	restriction from the left chart and a restriction from the right chart. -/
177	theorem exists_awayToOverlap_add (w : Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) :
178	    ∃ (p : Away 𝒜 (X 0)) (q : Away 𝒜 (X 1)),
179	      w = awayToOverlapLeft k p + awayToOverlapRight k q := by
180	  obtain ⟨f₁, f₂, hf⟩ := LaurentPolynomial.exists_toLaurent_add_aeval (overlapAlgEquiv k w)
181	  refine ⟨(awayAlgEquiv k fin_zero_ne_one).symm f₁,
182	    (awayAlgEquiv k fin_one_ne_zero).symm f₂, (overlapAlgEquiv k).injective ?_⟩
183	  rw [map_add, overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft, overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapRight,
184	    AlgEquiv.apply_symm_apply, AlgEquiv.apply_symm_apply, hf]
185	
186	/-! ### Section-level identifications -/
187	
188	theorem awayToSection_surjective {m : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (f_deg : f ∈ 𝒜 m)
189	    (hm : 0 < m) : Function.Surjective (Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 f).hom := fun z => by
190	  obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := (Proj.basicOpenIsoAway 𝒜 f f_deg hm).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.surjective z
191	  exact ⟨w, hw⟩
192	
193	theorem overlap_le_left : Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) ≤ chartOpen k 0 :=
194	  Proj.basicOpen_mono 𝒜 _ _ ⟨X 1, rfl⟩
195	
196	theorem overlap_le_right : Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) ≤ chartOpen k 1 :=
197	  Proj.basicOpen_mono 𝒜 _ _ ⟨X 0, mul_comm (X 0) (X 1)⟩
198	
199	theorem isAffineOpen_overlap : IsAffineOpen (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) :=
200	  Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen 𝒜 _ (X_mul_X_mem k) two_pos
201	
202	/-- Restriction of sections from the left chart to the overlap corresponds to
203	`P1.awayToOverlapLeft` under `Proj.awayToSection`. -/
204	theorem res_awayToSection_left (p : Away 𝒜 (X 0)) :
205	    ((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (overlap_le_left k)).op).hom
206	        ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom p) =
207	      (Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)).hom (awayToOverlapLeft k p) := by
208	  have h := Proj.awayMap_awayToSection 𝒜 (X_mem k 1)
209	    (rfl : (X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1 = X 0 * X 1)
210	  have h' := congr((CommRingCat.Hom.hom $h) p)
211	  simp only [CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.comp_apply, CommRingCat.hom_ofHom] at h'
212	  exact h'.symm
213	
214	/-- Restriction of sections from the right chart to the overlap corresponds to
215	`P1.awayToOverlapRight` under `Proj.awayToSection`. -/
216	theorem res_awayToSection_right (q : Away 𝒜 (X 1)) :
217	    ((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (overlap_le_right k)).op).hom
218	        ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom q) =
219	      (Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)).hom (awayToOverlapRight k q) := by
220	  have h := Proj.awayMap_awayToSection 𝒜 (X_mem k 0) (mul_comm (X 0) (X 1))
221	  have h' := congr((CommRingCat.Hom.hom $h) q)
222	  simp only [CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.comp_apply, CommRingCat.hom_ofHom] at h'
223	  exact h'.symm
224	
225	private theorem iso_symm_hom_apply {R S : CommRingCat.{u}} (e : R ≅ S) (x : R) :
226	    e.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.symm (e.hom.hom x) = x := by
227	  change e.inv.hom (e.hom.hom x) = x
228	  have h := congr((CommRingCat.Hom.hom $(e.hom_inv_id)) x)
229	  simp only [CommRingCat.hom_comp, CommRingCat.hom_id, RingHom.comp_apply,
230	    RingHom.id_apply] at h
231	  exact h
232	
233	/-- The identification of the section ring of the chart `D₊(X₀)` with `k[t]`, `t = X₁/X₀`. -/
234	noncomputable def chartSectionsEquiv₀ : Γ(P1 k, chartOpen k 0) ≃+* Polynomial k :=
235	  ((Proj.basicOpenIsoAway 𝒜 (X 0) (X_mem k 0) one_pos).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv).symm.trans
236	    (awayAlgEquiv k fin_zero_ne_one).toRingEquiv
237	
238	/-- The identification of the section ring of the chart `D₊(X₁)` with `k[t]`, `t = X₀/X₁`. -/
239	noncomputable def chartSectionsEquiv₁ : Γ(P1 k, chartOpen k 1) ≃+* Polynomial k :=
240	  ((Proj.basicOpenIsoAway 𝒜 (X 1) (X_mem k 1) one_pos).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv).symm.trans
241	    (awayAlgEquiv k fin_one_ne_zero).toRingEquiv
242	
243	/-- The identification of the section ring of the chart overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)` with the Laurent
244	polynomial ring, `T = X₁/X₀`. -/
245	noncomputable def overlapSectionsEquiv :
246	    Γ(P1 k, Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) ≃+* LaurentPolynomial k :=
247	  ((Proj.basicOpenIsoAway 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)
248	    (X_mul_X_mem k) two_pos).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv).symm.trans
249	    (overlapAlgEquiv k).toRingEquiv
250	
251	theorem chartSectionsEquiv₀_awayToSection (p : Away 𝒜 (X 0)) :
252	    chartSectionsEquiv₀ k ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom p) =
253	      awayAlgEquiv k fin_zero_ne_one p := by
254	  change (((Proj.basicOpenIsoAway 𝒜 (X 0) (X_mem k 0)
255	      one_pos).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv).symm.trans
256	      (awayAlgEquiv k fin_zero_ne_one).toRingEquiv)
257	      ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom p) = _
258	  rw [RingEquiv.trans_apply, ← Proj.basicOpenIsoAway_hom 𝒜 (X 0) (X_mem k 0) one_pos,
259	    iso_symm_hom_apply]
260	  rfl
261	
262	theorem chartSectionsEquiv₁_awayToSection (q : Away 𝒜 (X 1)) :
263	    chartSectionsEquiv₁ k ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom q) =
264	      awayAlgEquiv k fin_one_ne_zero q := by
265	  change (((Proj.basicOpenIsoAway 𝒜 (X 1) (X_mem k 1)
266	      one_pos).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv).symm.trans
267	      (awayAlgEquiv k fin_one_ne_zero).toRingEquiv)
268	      ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom q) = _
269	  rw [RingEquiv.trans_apply, ← Proj.basicOpenIsoAway_hom 𝒜 (X 1) (X_mem k 1) one_pos,
270	    iso_symm_hom_apply]
271	  rfl
272	
273	theorem overlapSectionsEquiv_awayToSection (w : Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) :
274	    overlapSectionsEquiv k ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)).hom w) =
275	      overlapAlgEquiv k w := by
276	  change (((Proj.basicOpenIsoAway 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)
277	      (X_mul_X_mem k) two_pos).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv).symm.trans
278	      (overlapAlgEquiv k).toRingEquiv)
279	      ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)).hom w) = _
280	  rw [RingEquiv.trans_apply, ← Proj.basicOpenIsoAway_hom 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)
281	    (X_mul_X_mem k) two_pos, iso_symm_hom_apply]
282	  rfl
283	
284	/-- Through the section-level identifications, restriction from the left chart to the
285	overlap is `t ↦ T`. -/
286	theorem overlapSectionsEquiv_res_left (a : Γ(P1 k, chartOpen k 0)) :
287	    overlapSectionsEquiv k (((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (overlap_le_left k)).op).hom a) =
288	      Polynomial.toLaurent (chartSectionsEquiv₀ k a) := by
289	  obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := awayToSection_surjective k (X 0) (X_mem k 0) one_pos a
290	  rw [res_awayToSection_left, overlapSectionsEquiv_awayToSection,
291	    chartSectionsEquiv₀_awayToSection, overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft]
292	
293	/-- Through the section-level identifications, restriction from the right chart to the
294	overlap is `t ↦ T⁻¹`. -/
295	theorem overlapSectionsEquiv_res_right (b : Γ(P1 k, chartOpen k 1)) :
296	    overlapSectionsEquiv k (((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (overlap_le_right k)).op).hom b) =
297	      Polynomial.aeval (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k)
298	        (chartSectionsEquiv₁ k b) := by
299	  obtain ⟨q, rfl⟩ := awayToSection_surjective k (X 1) (X_mem k 1) one_pos b
300	  rw [res_awayToSection_right, overlapSectionsEquiv_awayToSection,
301	    chartSectionsEquiv₁_awayToSection, overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapRight]
302	
303	end P1
304	
305	/-! ### The bundled chart package -/
306	
307	/-- A **Laurent chart pair** on the projective line over `k`: two affine opens covering
308	`P1 k` with a distinguished affine overlap, whose section rings are polynomial rings `k[t]`,
309	whose overlap section ring is the Laurent polynomial ring, and such that the two restriction
310	maps become `t ↦ T` and `t ↦ T⁻¹`.
311	
312	The canonical example is `P1.laurentChartPair k` (the two standard charts). The Laurent span
313	property `LaurentChartPair.exists_res_add_res` holds for any such pair; this package is
314	exactly what the two-lattice finiteness argument for `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` consumes. -/
315	structure LaurentChartPair (k : Type u) [Field k] where
316	  /-- The left chart. -/
317	  U₀ : (P1 k).Opens
318	  /-- The right chart. -/
319	  U₁ : (P1 k).Opens
320	  /-- The overlap. -/
321	  U₀₁ : (P1 k).Opens
322	  le_left : U₀₁ ≤ U₀
323	  le_right : U₀₁ ≤ U₁
324	  inf_eq : U₀ ⊓ U₁ = U₀₁
325	  isAffineOpen_U₀ : IsAffineOpen U₀
326	  isAffineOpen_U₁ : IsAffineOpen U₁
327	  isAffineOpen_U₀₁ : IsAffineOpen U₀₁
328	  /-- The two charts cover `P1 k`. -/
329	  sup_eq_top : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤
330	  /-- The sections on the left chart form a polynomial ring. -/
331	  Γ₀ : Γ(P1 k, U₀) ≃+* Polynomial k
332	  /-- The sections on the right chart form a polynomial ring. -/
333	  Γ₁ : Γ(P1 k, U₁) ≃+* Polynomial k
334	  /-- The sections on the overlap form a Laurent polynomial ring. -/
335	  Γ₀₁ : Γ(P1 k, U₀₁) ≃+* LaurentPolynomial k
336	  /-- Through the identifications, restriction from the left chart is `t ↦ T`. -/
337	  res_left : ∀ a, Γ₀₁ (((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE le_left).op).hom a) =
338	    Polynomial.toLaurent (Γ₀ a)
339	  /-- Through the identifications, restriction from the right chart is `t ↦ T⁻¹`. -/
340	  res_right : ∀ b, Γ₀₁ (((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE le_right).op).hom b) =
341	    Polynomial.aeval (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k) (Γ₁ b)
342	
343	namespace LaurentChartPair
344	
345	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (D : LaurentChartPair k)
346	
347	/-- **Laurent span** for any Laurent chart pair: every section on the overlap is the sum of a
348	restriction from the left chart and a restriction from the right chart. This is the
349	surjectivity half of the Mayer–Vietoris difference map for the two-chart cover. -/
350	theorem exists_res_add_res (z : Γ(P1 k, D.U₀₁)) :
351	    ∃ (a : Γ(P1 k, D.U₀)) (b : Γ(P1 k, D.U₁)),

43	instance cechPicSetoid (X : Scheme.{u}) : Setoid (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰) where
44	  r p q := ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1),
45	    unitsRes h₁ p.2 = unitsRes h₂ q.2

47	    constructor
48	    · exact fun p ↦ ⟨p.1, le_rfl, le_rfl, rfl⟩
49	    · rintro p q ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩

51	    · rintro p q r ⟨𝒲₁, h₁, h₂, e₁⟩ ⟨𝒲₂, h₃, h₄, e₂⟩
52	      refine ⟨𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂, inf_le_left.trans h₁, inf_le_right.trans h₄, ?_⟩

12	An **affine two-chart cover** of a scheme `Y` (`Scheme.AffineTwoCover`) is a pair of affine
13	opens `V₀, V₁` covering `Y` whose overlap `V₀ ⊓ V₁` is again affine. This file provides:

17	  `C/k` admits an affine two-chart cover (`Scheme.AffineTwoCover.nonempty_of_curve`), obtained

19	  (`exists_isFinite_toP1`, `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.MapToP1`); the overlap is affine because it
20	  is the preimage of the affine chart overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)`;
21	* **stability under base change**: an affine two-chart cover of `C.left` pulls back, along the
22	  first projection `(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left ⟶ C.left`, to an affine two-chart cover of
23	  `(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left`, for any `k`-algebra `R` (`Scheme.AffineTwoCover.pullbackProd`).

25	  `overSpec k R ⟶ Spec k` (itself affine, being a morphism between affine schemes) along

27	  morphism are affine.
